# Why Ugayafukiaezu is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *ugayafukiaezu*. This is the file on how **Ugayafukiaezu** replaced it.

Ugayafukiaezu's mythology is the final chapter of the Hoori-Toyotama story and the prelude to the reign of Jimmu.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Ugayafukiaezu
- **ASCII form:** ugayafukiaezu
- **Meaning:** "Cormorant grass-thatching unfinished"
- **Domain of influence:** Ancestor of Jimmu
- **Pantheon:** Japanese
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** 鵜草葺不合命
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 499 of 542

## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **鵜草葺不合命**, in the attestation Kojiki (Hoori, Toyotama, and Ugayafukiaezu cycle) and Nihon Shoki (parallel genealogy) give us. On the evidence, it means "Cormorant grass-thatching unfinished".


Spoken, the name runs `/ɯ.ɡa.ja.fɯ.ki.a.e.zɯ/` — 'OO-gah-yah-foo-kee-ah-eh-zoo' — many light syllables; the 'f' is soft, made with both lips.

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Ugayafukiaezu** lives at [/ugayafukiaezu/](/ugayafukiaezu/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/ugayafukiaezu/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/ugayafukiaezu/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/ugayafukiaezu/patterns/).

One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

## Where the Name Stood First

Ugayafukiaezu has no independent material cult. His significance is textual and genealogical, preserved in the Kojiki's account of the imperial lineage. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **3 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Ancestry & Heritage Services** (the cormorant-grass prince and father of Jimmu; Japanese imperial ancestry begins here.); **Leadership, Governance & Public Administration** (ancestor of the first emperor; imperial leadership begins with him.); **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries** (born of the sea-foam and cormorant-thatched palace; the maritime ancestor of Jimmu.). The [Resonance File](/ugayafukiaezu/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

The Japanese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Kojiki](/texts/kojiki/) and [Nihon Shoki](/texts/nihon-shoki/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
